A beluga needs many years before it spawns for the first time. That is why stocks recover only very slowly.

teile.einleitung: Helsinki is the capital and largest city of Finland. It lies in the south of the country on the Baltic Sea. The city is known for its white cathedral, the sea fortress of Suomenlinna and modern design.
wichtigste: Helsinki is the capital of Finland.
The city lies on the Gulf of Finland, a part of the Baltic Sea.
Helsinki Cathedral is white and has green domes.
Suomenlinna is an old sea fortress and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
In 1952 the Summer Olympics took place in Helsinki.
The street signs are in Finnish and Swedish.
Helsinki was founded in 1550 by the Swedish king.

abschnitte.text: For centuries Finland belonged to the kingdom of **Sweden**. The Swedish king **Gustav I Vasa** founded Helsinki in 1550 as a trading town. Later Finland came under Russian rule. At that time, in 1812, Helsinki became the capital. Since 1917 Finland has been an independent state, and Helsinki has remained its capital.

The best-known building is **Helsinki Cathedral**. It is white and has green domes. The cathedral stands at the top of a large flight of steps above **Senate Square**. Around the square stand more buildings in the same style, designed by the architect Carl Ludvig Engel. That is why the city centre looks very uniform and bright.

Off Helsinki lies **Suomenlinna**, a fortress on several islands. It was built in the 18th century, when Finland still belonged to Sweden, to protect the coast. Today people live there, and there are museums, cafés and old walls to explore. Suomenlinna is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. By ferry you are there in a few minutes.

Finland has two **official languages**: Finnish and Swedish. That is why the street names in Helsinki are in both languages. In Swedish the city is called **Helsingfors**. Most people in Helsinki speak Finnish as their mother tongue, and a minority speak Swedish. As in Switzerland, then, there are several official languages in the same country.

In 1952 the **Summer Olympics** took place in Helsinki. The Olympic Stadium with its tall white tower still stands today. Many **ferries** sail from the harbour across the Baltic Sea. They go especially often to **Tallinn**, the capital of Estonia. The crossing takes only about two hours. There are also ferries to Stockholm.

gewusst: In winter the sea off Helsinki can freeze, and then icebreakers help the ships.
There are very many saunas in Finland, and in Helsinki there are public saunas right by the sea.

teile.einleitung: The Baltic Sea is a sea in the north of Europe between Scandinavia and the rest of the mainland. It is a young sea with water that is only slightly salty and almost no ebb and flow.
wichtigste: Nine states border the Baltic Sea, for example Germany, Sweden, Poland and Finland.
The water is much less salty than the water in the Mediterranean.
There is hardly any tide.
On the beach you often find amber.
In winter the northern part often freezes over.
The Kiel Canal links the Baltic Sea with the North Sea.

abschnitte.text: The Baltic Sea lies, for example, between **Germany** and **Sweden**. Nine states lie on it: Germany, Denmark, Sweden, Finland, Russia, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania and Poland. Countries on a sea are called **riparian states**. The Baltic Sea is a very **young** sea. It formed in its present shape **after the last ice age**, when the glaciers melted about 10,000 years ago.

Into the Baltic Sea flow many rivers with **fresh water**. It is connected with the North Sea only by narrow straits. That is why its water is much **less salty** than in the Mediterranean. Such water is called **brackish water**. There are also almost no **tides**: with ebb and flow the water level changes by only a few centimetres. In the far north the slightly salty water freezes easily in winter, and then it is covered with **ice**.

On the beaches of the Baltic Sea you often find **amber**. This is very old, hardened **tree resin** from forests that grew millions of years ago. The waves wash the golden-yellow pieces onto the beach. Sometimes small insects are even trapped inside.

Many people take seaside holidays on the Baltic Sea. Out of the wind they sit in a **beach basket chair**, a seat of wickerwork with a roof. It was invented in **1882** in **Rostock**. For a long time a lot of **herring** has also been caught in the Baltic Sea, an important food fish that lives in large shoals.

The **Kiel Canal** runs right across northern Germany from the North Sea to the Baltic Sea. Ships thereby save the long way around **Denmark**. It is among the busiest artificial waterways in the world.

gewusst: Amber is so light that it almost floats in salt water.
Because the water is so little salty, sea fish and freshwater fish live side by side in the Baltic Sea.

teile.einleitung: The Moldavian monasteries stand in Bukovina in the north of Romania. Their churches are painted with coloured pictures completely, not only inside but also outside.
wichtigste: The Moldavian monasteries lie in Bukovina in the north of Romania.
The churches are painted all over on the outside with pictures from the Bible.
The paintings date from the 15th and 16th centuries.
Several of the churches are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
Especially well known is Voroneț Monastery with its glowing blue.

abschnitte.text: In the region of **Bukovina** in the north of Romania stand several monasteries with very special churches. Their **outer walls** are painted all over with coloured pictures. The paintings show stories from the **Bible**, saints and scenes from the faith. They date from the 15th and 16th centuries. At that time the area belonged to the principality of **Moldavia**, hence the name.

At that time many people could not read. The pictures on the walls told them the stories of the faith, like a picture book. Many of the churches were built under Prince **Stephen the Great** and his son **Petru Rareș**. It is astonishing that many colours are still well preserved after almost 500 years of wind and weather.

Especially well known is **Voroneț** Monastery. Its glowing blue is also called “Voroneț blue”. Other famous churches stand at **Sucevița**, **Humor** and **Moldovița**. Since 1993 several of these churches have been part of the **UNESCO World Heritage**. In many monasteries nuns or monks still live today.

gewusst: Because of its paintings, Voroneț Monastery is sometimes called the “Sistine Chapel of the East”.

teile.einleitung: A heatwave is a period of several days or weeks with unusually high temperatures. In Europe, heatwaves have become more frequent and stronger in recent decades. They can be dangerous for people, animals and forests.
wichtigste: A heatwave is a longer period with very high temperatures.
The European heat record is 48.8 degrees, measured in 2021 in Sicily.
The Swiss record of 41.5 degrees was measured in Grono in 2003.
The 2003 heatwave claimed over 70,000 lives in Europe.
A blocking high often causes long heatwaves.
A tropical night is a night when the temperature does not fall below 20 degrees.
Cities cool down less at night, which is called the urban heat island effect.

abschnitte.text: Behind a heatwave there is often a **blocking high**. A high-pressure area like this stays in the same place for days and steers the lows with rain around the outside. On the weather map it sometimes looks like the Greek letter omega, so people speak of an **omega block**. In a high, the air sinks and warms up as it does so. At the same time the Sun shines almost without clouds and keeps heating the ground more and more.

On 11 August 2021, 48.8 degrees was measured at Floridia near **Syracuse** in Sicily. The World Meteorological Organization has recognised this value as the **European record**. Spain holds its record with 47.6 degrees, measured on 14 August 2021 in **La Rambla** near Córdoba (as of 2026). In Portugal, **Amareleja** in the Alentejo reached about 47.3 degrees on 1 August 2003.

The summer of 2003 brought one of the worst heatwaves in European history. Studies estimate that **over 70,000 more people** died than usual. Older people were especially affected, for example in Italy, France and Spain. In Switzerland, 41.5 degrees was measured on 11 August 2003 in **Grono** in the Misox valley (Grisons). To this day that is the highest value ever measured in Switzerland (as of 2026).

People speak of a **tropical night** when the temperature does not fall below 20 degrees at night. Many nights like this are exhausting, because the body cannot recover properly during sleep. In big cities such as Athens this is especially common. The reason is the **urban heat island effect**: asphalt, concrete and dense buildings store heat during the day and give it off again at night. There are also fewer trees and meadows, which cool the air through evaporation.

Heatwaves have many consequences. In July 2023 the **Acropolis** in Athens was closed on the hottest afternoons to protect visitors and staff. On the island of **Rhodes**, large forest fires broke out in the same month, and thousands of holidaymakers had to be brought to safety, some of them by boat. In the heat it helps to drink a lot, stay in the shade and spend the hottest hours indoors. In Switzerland, **MeteoSwiss** warns of dangerous heat.

gewusst: Experts expect heatwaves in Europe to become even more frequent because of climate change.
The heat of the summer of 2003 also made many glaciers in the Alps melt especially strongly.

teile.einleitung: The Ljubljanica is a river in Slovenia. It flows right through the old town of the capital, Ljubljana. On its banks lie many cafés and famous bridges.
wichtigste: The Ljubljanica flows right through the old town of Ljubljana.
It divides the old town into two halves.
Many bridges cross the river, such as the Dragon Bridge and the Triple Bridge.
The Ljubljanica is a karst river and flows partly underground.
It flows into the Sava.

abschnitte.text: The Ljubljanica is a **karst river**. **Karst** is a landscape of limestone in which water washes out caves and underground passages. The water of the Ljubljanica therefore disappears into the ground several times and comes up again at another place. Each time the river has a different name. That is why it is also called the **river with seven names**. After Ljubljana it flows into the **Sava**.

In **Ljubljana**, the capital of **Slovenia**, the Ljubljanica divides the old town into **two halves**. On its banks lie many **cafés** and markets. The **Triple Bridge**, three bridges right next to each other, is well known. The **Dragon Bridge** is decorated with figures of dragons, because the **dragon** is the heraldic animal of the city.

Many banks and bridges along the Ljubljanica were designed in the 20th century by the Slovenian architect **Jože Plečnik**. Among other things he extended the Triple Bridge. His buildings shape the look of the city to this day. Since 2021 they have been part of the **UNESCO World Heritage**.

gewusst: On its way the Ljubljanica disappears underground several times and comes out again with a new name.

teile.einleitung: Mljet is a long, wooded island in Dalmatia in the south of Croatia. In the west of the island lies a national park with two saltwater lakes and an old monastery on a small island.
wichtigste: Mljet is an island in southern Dalmatia, not far from Dubrovnik.
A large part of the island is covered with forest.
In the national park lie the Great Lake and the Small Lake.
The lakes are connected to the sea and contain salt water.
On an island in the Great Lake stands an old monastery.

abschnitte.text: **Mljet** lies in the Adriatic off the coast of southern Dalmatia, not far from **Dubrovnik**. The island is long and narrow and largely covered with **forest**, mainly pine trees. There are only a few small villages. Many visitors come by boat for a day trip.

In the west of the island lies a **national park**. There are two lakes there: the **Great Lake** and the **Small Lake**. They are connected to the **sea** by narrow channels, so they contain **salt water**. The water is often warmer than in the open sea, and you can swim in it. Around the lakes run hiking and cycling paths.

In the middle of the Great Lake lies a small island with an old **monastery** and a church. Monks of the Benedictine order founded it in the Middle Ages. You can cross to it in a small boat. The island in the lake on the island in the sea is an especially pretty subject for photographs.

gewusst: On Mljet there is an island in a lake that itself lies on an island.

teile.einleitung: North Macedonia is a small landlocked country in the south of the Balkan Peninsula. The capital is Skopje, and since 2019 the country has had its present name.
wichtigste: The capital and largest city is Skopje on the River Vardar.
In 1963 Skopje was badly destroyed by a severe earthquake.
Since 2019 the country has officially been called North Macedonia.
The change of name rests on an agreement with Greece.
The currency is the Macedonian denar.
Lake Ohrid is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

abschnitte.text: The capital of **North Macedonia** is **Skopje**. It lies on the River **Vardar** and is the largest city in the country. In **1963** a severe **earthquake** destroyed large parts of the city. Afterwards it was rebuilt with help from many countries. In Skopje **Mother Teresa** was also born in 1910.

The country used to belong to **Yugoslavia** and became independent in **1991**. For a long time it was called **Macedonia**. The neighbouring country **Greece** rejected this name, because a Greek region is also called that. After an **agreement** between the two countries, the country has officially been called **North Macedonia** since **2019**. After that it was able to join NATO in 2020.

In North Macedonia people pay with the **Macedonian denar**. In the neighbouring country of **Serbia** the currency has a similar name, namely **dinar**. Both names derive from the Roman denarius, an old silver coin. Anyone coming from Switzerland has to change their francs.

North Macedonia has **no sea coast**, but many mountains. In the south-west lies **Lake Ohrid**, one of the oldest lakes in the world. The town of **Ohrid** on the lake is famous for its old churches. The region around the lake is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

gewusst: Lake Ohrid is probably over a million years old and so one of the oldest lakes in Europe.
North Macedonia is a good half the size of Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Maribor is the second largest city in Slovenia and lies on the Drava. The city is famous for its “Old Vine”, the oldest vine in the world that still bears fruit.
wichtigste: Maribor is the second largest city in Slovenia.
The city lies on the River Drava.
The “Old Vine” in Maribor is over 400 years old.
It is regarded as the oldest grapevine in the world that still bears fruit.
In 2012 Maribor was European Capital of Culture.

abschnitte.text: On an old house in the **Lent** district on the bank of the Drava grows the **Old Vine**. It is over 400 years old and still bears grapes. That is why it is recorded as the **oldest fruit-bearing grapevine in the world**. Every year its grapes are harvested at a small festival. From cuttings of the vine, plants now grow in other cities.

Maribor lies in the north-east of Slovenia on the **Drava**, a river that comes from the Alps. The old town has squares, churches and old houses. Around the city lie many **vineyards**, because the area is a well-known wine-growing region. In **2012** Maribor was **European Capital of Culture**.

Right next to the city begins the wooded mountain range of **Pohorje**. In winter you can ski there. For decades women's **Alpine Ski World Cup** races have also been held here. In summer Pohorje is popular with hikers and cyclists.

gewusst: The Old Vine in Maribor is older than most of the houses in the city.

teile.einleitung: The Curonian Spit is a long, narrow strip of sand on the Baltic Sea. It separates the Curonian Lagoon from the open sea and is known for its huge moving dunes. Since 2000 it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
wichtigste: The Curonian Spit is about 98 kilometres long.
The northern part belongs to Lithuania, the southern part to the Russian region of Kaliningrad.
Between the spit and the mainland lies the Curonian Lagoon, a shallow lagoon.
The highest moving dunes are over 50 metres high.
At its narrowest point the spit is only about 400 metres wide.
Since 2000 it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

abschnitte.text: A **spit** is a narrow strip of sand that almost cuts off a bay from the sea. The Curonian Spit is about **98 kilometres** long. It runs from Zelenogradsk in the south to opposite Klaipėda in the north. At its narrowest point it is only about 400 metres wide, and at its widest just under 4 kilometres.

Waves often hit the beach at an **angle**. In doing so they move the sand step by step along the coast. This is called **longshore drift**. Where the coast bends, the sand is deposited in a hook that keeps growing. This is how the spit formed, and behind it the **Curonian Lagoon**, a large, shallow **lagoon**.

On the spit there are some of the highest **moving dunes** in Europe. The big dunes near Nida and Pervalka are over 50 metres high. The wind slowly pushes the sand along, which is why the dunes “move”. In the past the forests were cut down, and the dunes buried several villages. In the **19th century** people planted **marram grass** and **pine trees** to hold the sand in place again.

abschnitte.titel: Two countries, one World Heritage Site
abschnitte.text: The northern part of the spit belongs to **Lithuania**, the southern part to the Russian region of **Kaliningrad**. Near Klaipėda the lagoon is joined to the Baltic Sea by a narrow opening. In **2000** **UNESCO** added the spit to the World Heritage List as a **cultural landscape**. This protects nature and the work of people together.

gewusst: Without the replanting in the 19th century, even more villages would have disappeared under the sand.
In autumn huge flocks of migrating birds pass over the spit.

teile.einleitung: The Netherlands is a flat country in north-western Europe on the North Sea. A large part lies lower than the sea and is protected by dykes.
wichtigste: The capital is Amsterdam, but the government and parliament sit in The Hague.
Many people say “Holland”, but that is only a region in the west.
About a quarter of the country lies below sea level.
Dykes protect the land from the water.
In the Netherlands there are more bicycles than inhabitants.
Rotterdam has the largest seaport in Europe.

abschnitte.text: The **Netherlands** lies on the **North Sea** between Belgium and Germany. The capital is **Amsterdam**, but the **government** and **parliament** work in **The Hague**. The **king** also lives there, because the country is a kingdom. Many people say **“Holland”** for the whole country. But Holland is really only a region in the west with two provinces.

About **a quarter** of the country lies **below sea level**. Without protection the sea would flood these areas. That is why there are long, high **dykes** of earth along the coast and the rivers. In the past **windmills** pumped the water out of the fields, and today pumping stations do that. Newly won land is called a **polder**.

The country is flat and has very many cycle paths. There are even **more bicycles than inhabitants**. At sporting events fans wear **orange**. This is the colour of the royal family, which comes from the **House of Orange**. On King's Day the whole country is decorated in orange.

The town of **Gouda** gave its name to a well-known **cheese**, as cheese has long been traded there. The traditional wooden shoes are called **klompen** and are carved from a single piece of **wood**. In the past farmers wore them on wet fields. Also famous are the colourful **tulip fields** in spring.

**Rotterdam** has the **largest seaport in Europe**. Ships from all over the world arrive here. Many goods travel from there on ships up the **Rhine** as far as **Basel**. The national language is **Dutch**. It is related to German, so some words sound similar.

gewusst: Schiphol airport near Amsterdam lies several metres below sea level.
The windmills of Kinderdijk are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

teile.einleitung: The Catalans are a people in the north-east of Spain, with their own language and culture. Most of them live in the region of Catalonia, whose capital is Barcelona. For years there has been a dispute over whether Catalonia should become independent.
wichtigste: The Catalans speak Catalan, a Romance language of its own.
The regional government is called the Generalitat de Catalunya.
The national day, the Diada, on 11 September recalls the fall of Barcelona in 1714.
On 1 October 2017 a disputed independence referendum took place.
The human towers, the castells, have been UNESCO cultural heritage since 2010.
In Alghero on Sardinia a form of Catalan is still spoken today.

abschnitte.text: **Catalan** is a Romance language of its own, related to Spanish, French and Italian. It is spoken in Catalonia, but also in Valencia, on the Balearic Islands and in **Andorra**. In the town of **Alghero** on Sardinia, some people still speak Catalan today. The town had been conquered by the Crown of Aragon in the 14th century and settled with Catalans.

In the **War of the Spanish Succession**, Bourbon troops captured **Barcelona** on 11 September 1714. After that Catalonia lost its own institutions. The **Diada**, the Catalan national day on 11 September, recalls this event. The regional government, the **Generalitat de Catalunya**, goes back to a medieval institution. It was restored after the end of the Franco dictatorship, and its seat is the Palau de la Generalitat in Barcelona.

Many Catalans want more self-government or a state of their own, while others want to stay with **Spain**. On **1 October 2017** a **referendum** on independence took place, although the Spanish Constitutional Court had banned it. There were police operations. After that the government in Madrid temporarily took control of the regional government. The question is still disputed today.

A well-known tradition is the **castells**, the human towers. Groups climb on top of each other and form towers of up to ten levels. At the very top there is often a child wearing a helmet. The motto is strength, balance, courage and good sense. Since **2010** the castells have been part of UNESCO's **intangible cultural heritage**.

gewusst: In Andorra Catalan is the only official language.
On the day of Saint George, 23 April, people in Catalonia give each other roses and books.

teile.einleitung: The Great Hungarian Plain is a huge, flat landscape in the east and south of Hungary. In Hungarian it is called the Alföld. It has wide steppes, fields and the River Tisza.
wichtigste: The Hungarian name of the plain is Alföld, which means roughly “lowland”.
It takes up about half of the area of Hungary.
The Tisza is its most important river.
The steppe with few trees is called the puszta.
In 1973 the Hortobágy became Hungary's first national park.
The plain belongs to the Pannonian Basin.

abschnitte.text: The **Great Hungarian Plain** is called **Alföld** in Hungarian, which means roughly “lowland”. It stretches across the east and south of Hungary and takes up about **half of the country's area**. Parts of it also reach into neighbouring countries such as Serbia and Romania. The landscape is very flat. The warm, sunny climate is well suited to growing crops.

The **Tisza** flows through the plain from north to south. It rises in the Carpathians in Ukraine and flows into the **Danube** in Serbia. It is the longest tributary of the Danube. From **1846** the Tisza was straightened and embanked under **István Széchenyi** and the engineer **Pál Vásárhelyi**. As a result, huge marshy areas became farmland, but many **wetlands** were lost.

The **puszta** is a wide, dry **grass steppe** with few trees. It arose partly naturally and partly through clearing and grazing. Typical features are **sweep wells** and herders with herds of cattle and horses. The grey **Hungarian Grey cattle** with long, curved horns used to be driven in large herds as far as western Europe. The **Hortobágy** near Debrecen became Hungary's first national park in **1973** and has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** since 1999.

The plain belongs to the **Pannonian Basin**, which is surrounded by the Carpathians, the Alps and the Dinarides. A few million years ago an **inland sea**, the **Pannonian Sea**, lay here. Its deposits and later river sediments now form the flat ground beneath.

In the south of the plain a lot of **spice paprika** is grown. The towns of **Szeged** and **Kalocsa** are especially well known for it. Both even have their own paprika museums. Paprika is one of the most important spices in Hungarian cooking, for example in goulash.

gewusst: The Hortobágy is considered the largest continuous steppe in central Europe.
Where there are fields today, there was a sea millions of years ago.

teile.einleitung: The Morava is an important river in Serbia. It flows north through the middle of the country and flows into the Danube near Smederevo.
wichtigste: The Morava is also called the Great Morava.
It forms from two source rivers.
The source rivers are called the West Morava and the South Morava.
The Morava flows north through central Serbia.
Near Smederevo it flows into the Danube.

abschnitte.titel: A river made of two rivers
abschnitte.text: The **Morava** is more precisely called the **Great Morava**. It forms where two rivers meet: the **West Morava** and the **South Morava**. From there it flows north through **central Serbia**. Near the town of **Smederevo**, east of Belgrade, it flows into the **Danube**. So its water ends up in the Black Sea.

The broad **valley of the Morava** has always been an important **transport route** through Serbia. Even in Roman times a road ran through here. Today a motorway and a railway line run through the valley. They link central Europe with Greece and Turkey.

In the **Czech Republic** there is also a river with the name Morava. In German this river is called the **March**, and the region of **Moravia** is named after it. It has nothing to do with the Serbian Morava, though. Both rivers do, however, end up flowing into the Danube.

gewusst: The Danube, into which the Morava flows, is after the Volga the second longest river in Europe.

teile.einleitung: The Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea between Great Britain and Ireland. It belongs to the British Crown, but is not part of the United Kingdom. The island has its own parliament and its own laws.
wichtigste: The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea.
It belongs to the British Crown, but not to the United Kingdom.
It also does not belong to the European Union.
Its parliament is called Tynwald.
Its emblem is three legs in a circle.

abschnitte.text: The Isle of Man is a so-called **Crown dependency**. This means that the British king or queen is also the ruler of the island, where they hold the title “Lord of Mann”. But the island belongs neither to the **United Kingdom** nor to the **EU**. It manages its own affairs itself. Great Britain is responsible for defence and foreign policy.

The island's parliament is called **Tynwald**. It is regarded as one of the oldest parliaments in the world that has existed without a break. Its roots go back to the time of the **Vikings**, who once ruled the island. Once a year, on the national holiday in July, it gathers in the open air on a hill. There the new laws are announced publicly.

The emblem of the island is **three legs** in armour arranged in a circle. It is called the triskelion and can also be seen on the flag. The island is known for the **Manx cat**, a breed of cat that often has no tail. The motorcycle race **Isle of Man TT**, which is run on normal roads of the island, is also famous. The old language of the island is called **Manx**, a Celtic language.

gewusst: The Isle of Man has its own stamps and its own banknotes and coins, the Manx pound.
The island's national day, Tynwald Day, is on 5 July.

teile.einleitung: Madeira is a Portuguese island in the Atlantic, far off the coast of Africa. It is known for its hiking trails along water channels, its ancient laurel forest and Madeira wine.
wichtigste: Madeira belongs to Portugal and lies in the Atlantic.
The capital is called Funchal.
Narrow water channels, the levadas, run across the island.
The laurel forest has been a UNESCO natural World Heritage Site since 1999.
The fortified wine Madeira is named after the island.

abschnitte.text: Madeira was formed by **volcanoes** and has steep mountains and deep gorges. The island belongs to **Portugal**, but lies closer to Africa than to the Portuguese mainland. The capital, **Funchal**, lies on the south coast. It is famous for its great **New Year's Eve fireworks** over the harbour. Thanks to the mild climate, flowers bloom on Madeira all year round.

In the north of the island it rains a lot, and in the south it is drier. That is why the inhabitants built narrow **irrigation channels**, the **levadas**, centuries ago. They carry water from the mountains to fields and villages in the south. Together they are over 2000 kilometres long. Beside many levadas run narrow paths on which you can hike today. Similar channels exist in the canton of **Valais**, where they are called suonen.

In the damp mountains grows the **laurel forest**, also called **Laurisilva**. It is a remnant of forests that were widespread in southern Europe millions of years ago. On Madeira it has survived especially well. Since 1999 it has been a **UNESCO natural World Heritage Site**. In the forest mist and moss often hang, and many plants occur only here.

A well-known **fortified wine** is named after the island. Madeira wine is warmed as it matures and therefore keeps for a very long time. In the past ships took it on long voyages, because it did not spoil in the heat. It is of course not for children, but it has made the island world famous.

gewusst: The footballer Cristiano Ronaldo was born in Funchal on Madeira.
Some levadas lead through dark tunnels, for which hikers need a torch.

teile.einleitung: Northern Ireland is a part of the United Kingdom in the north-east of the island of Ireland. Well known are the capital Belfast, where the Titanic was built, and the basalt columns of the Giant's Causeway.
wichtigste: Northern Ireland belongs to the United Kingdom.
The capital and largest city is Belfast.
The Titanic was built at the Harland and Wolff shipyard in Belfast.
The Giant's Causeway consists of about 40,000 basalt columns.
Lough Neagh is the largest lake in the United Kingdom.

abschnitte.text: The island of **Ireland** is divided: the largest part is the independent state of Ireland, and the north-east is called **Northern Ireland**. Northern Ireland, like England, Scotland and Wales, belongs to the **United Kingdom**. People pay there with the **pound**, and in Ireland with the euro. For a long time there was a serious conflict in Northern Ireland between different groups of the population. With the **Good Friday Agreement** of 1998 a peace process was agreed.

The capital and largest city is **Belfast**. It lies at the mouth of the River **Lagan**. In Belfast the **Titanic** was built at the **Harland and Wolff** shipyard. The ship sank in **1912** on her first voyage. Today a large museum in Belfast recalls the Titanic.

On the north coast lies the **Giant's Causeway**. It consists of about **40,000 basalt columns**, many of them hexagonal. They formed when **lava** slowly cooled millions of years ago and cracked as it did so. A legend tells that a giant built the causeway. The place is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

At about **390 square kilometres**, **Lough Neagh** is the largest lake by area in the United Kingdom. That makes it about two thirds the size of Lake Geneva, but much less deep. The lake supplies a large part of the **drinking water** for Northern Ireland. Many eels are also caught in it.

gewusst: Some basalt columns of the Giant's Causeway are over 10 metres high.
Parts of the television series “Game of Thrones” were filmed in Northern Ireland.

teile.einleitung: The Lysefjord is a long, narrow fjord in south-west Norway near Stavanger. Above it rises the famous rock platform Preikestolen, a popular hiking destination.
wichtigste: The Lysefjord lies in south-west Norway, near the city of Stavanger.
It is about 40 kilometres long and surrounded by steep rock walls.
The rock slab Preikestolen lies about 600 metres above the water.
A fjord is an arm of the sea that glaciers have scoured out.

abschnitte.text: A **fjord** is a long, narrow arm of the sea that reaches far inland. It formed in the ice age, when **glaciers** scoured out deep valleys. When the ice melted, seawater flowed into the valleys. The Lysefjord is about 40 kilometres long. In many places the rock walls rise almost vertically out of the water.

The best-known sight is **Preikestolen**, which means Pulpit Rock in English. It is a large, flat **rock slab** about 600 metres above the fjord. The hiking trail there takes a few hours there and back. At the top you have a wide view over the fjord. Because there is no fence, you have to be very careful at the edge.

Many visitors explore the Lysefjord by **boat**. From the water you can see the mighty walls and waterfalls. Further inside the fjord lies the **Kjeragbolten**, a large boulder wedged between two rock walls, high above the water.

gewusst: Preikestolen often appears in films and photographs because the view is so spectacular.

teile.einleitung: The Øresund Bridge links Denmark and Sweden. It crosses the Øresund, a strait between Copenhagen and Malmö. Cars and trains travel on it at the same time.
wichtigste: The Øresund link opened on 1 July 2000.
The bridge itself is about 8 kilometres long, and the whole link about 16 kilometres.
Part of it runs through a tunnel under the sea.
Cars drive on top, and trains run below.
The main part is a cable-stayed bridge with pylons about 200 metres high.
It links the Danish island of Zealand with Scania in Sweden.

abschnitte.text: Before the year 2000 you could only cross between Denmark and Sweden at this spot by **ferry**. On 1 July 2000 the **Øresund link** was opened. It links **Copenhagen** on the island of **Zealand** with **Malmö** in **Scania**, the southernmost region of Sweden.

The whole link is about 16 kilometres long. It consists of three parts: the actual **bridge** of about 7.8 kilometres, an artificial **island** called Peberholm, and a **tunnel**. The tunnel was needed because tall bridge piers would have interfered with the nearby **Copenhagen Airport**. In addition, large ships can in this way pass unhindered through the Øresund.
The bridge has two levels. On the upper deck runs a **motorway**, and on the lower the **railway**. So cars and trains can cross at the same time. Many people live on one side and work on the other.

The main part is a **cable-stayed bridge**. In this, steel cables carry the roadway. They are stretched at an angle from tall towers, the **pylons**, to the roadway. The pylons of the Øresund Bridge are about 200 metres high. The bridge is among the best-known structures in Scandinavia.

gewusst: The island of Peberholm was specially built up for the link and is now a habitat for many plants and birds.
The bridge is so well known that it gave its name to a television crime series.

teile.einleitung: The maquis is a dense, evergreen scrubland in the Mediterranean region. It mostly arose where people in the past cleared or overused forests of holm oaks.
wichtigste: The maquis is evergreen scrub in the Mediterranean region.
The shrubs usually grow about 1 to 3 metres high.
It mostly arose from destroyed holm oak forests.
With even heavier overuse, rocky heath forms, called garrigue in France.
Similar scrubland exists in California (chaparral) and South Africa (fynbos).
In Italian the maquis is called “macchia”.

abschnitte.text: In the past, **hard-leaved forests** with **holm oaks** grew in many areas around the Mediterranean. Since antiquity people have destroyed these forests by slash-and-burn clearing, logging and grazing by goats and sheep. In their place grew the dense, **evergreen scrub** of the maquis. The shrubs usually grow 1 to 3 metres high. Scrub woodland from overused oak forests can reach 3 to 5 metres.

Many plants of the maquis have small, hard and leathery leaves. This way they lose little water in the dry summer. They are called **sclerophyllous plants**. Typical are myrtle, tree heath, mastic and the **strawberry tree**. Its red, warty fruits recall strawberries, are edible and ripen in autumn and winter. Many shrubs smell strongly of essential oils.

If the maquis burns down again and again, **rockroses** spread, because their seeds germinate especially well after a fire. Other species can then hardly recover. If the land is grazed even more heavily and the soil is washed away, a low, stony **rocky heath** forms. In France it is called **garrigue**, in Spain tomillares and in Greece **phrygana**.

Elsewhere too there is a climate with dry summers and wet winters. In California the **chaparral** grows there, and in South Africa the **fynbos**. These scrublands look similar to the maquis, although they have hardly any species in common. The similar climate has produced similar adaptations independently of each other. This is called **convergent evolution**.

The French word for the scrubland is **maquis**. In the Second World War fighters of the French Resistance often hid in this hard-to-reach scrubland. That is why they were called **Maquisards**. On the island of Corsica in particular the maquis is still a defining feature of the landscape.

gewusst: The seeds of rockroses germinate better after a fire than before.
The French name maquis comes from the Italian word macchia.

teile.einleitung: Coastal erosion means that the sea wears away the coast bit by bit. Waves, currents, wind and rain gnaw at beaches and rocks. In Europe people try to protect coasts in various ways.
wichtigste: The Holderness coast in Yorkshire retreats by about 1.5 to 2 metres every year.
It consists of soft boulder clay from the last ice age.
Groynes slow the transport of sand along the beach.
On Sylt sand is regularly pumped onto the beach.
The Sand Engine near The Hague is an artificial sand peninsula from 2011.
Sea walls can increase erosion on neighbouring beaches.

abschnitte.titel: How the sea wears away the coast
abschnitte.text: **Erosion** means wearing away. On the coast, **waves** crash against beaches and cliffs and loosen material. The **current** carries sand further along the coast. Soft rock disappears much faster than hard rock. Frost and rain also help to loosen rocks.

The **Holderness coast** in Yorkshire in England retreats by about **1.5 to 2 metres** every year, faster than any other in Europe. The cliffs consist of loose **boulder clay** that glaciers deposited in the last ice age. Every year about 2 million tonnes of material are lost there. Since Roman times at least **23 places** have vanished into the sea.

On **Heligoland** stands the **Lange Anna**, a freestanding sea stack of red **Bunter sandstone** about 47 metres high. The surf gnaws at its foot. On the island of **Rügen** the **Wissower Klinken** largely collapsed into the sea in February **2005**. These chalk cliffs were a popular photo spot in Jasmund National Park.

**Groynes** are walls of wood or stone built out into the sea at right angles to the beach. They catch the sand that the current carries along the coast. **Sea walls** also protect the land behind them. But they have a drawback: behind the wall no more material is worn away, and the **neighbouring beaches** lack this sand. They are therefore eroded more strongly.

On the west coast of **Sylt**, special ships have pumped about a million cubic metres of sand onto the beach every year since the 1970s. This is called **beach nourishment**. In the Netherlands the **Sand Engine** was built near The Hague in **2011**: a hook-shaped peninsula of about **21.5 million cubic metres** of sand. Currents and wind gradually spread this sand onto nearby beaches.

gewusst: The Sand Engine is meant to supply the Dutch coast with sand for about 20 years.
On the Holderness coast whole medieval villages now lie under the sea.

teile.einleitung: The Lake District is a landscape of mountains and lakes in the north-west of England. It is a national park and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Poets and children's authors have lived and written here.
wichtigste: The Lake District lies in the county of Cumbria in the north-west of England.
It has been a national park since 1951 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2017.
At 978 metres, Scafell Pike is the highest mountain in England.
Windermere is the largest natural lake in England.
Ice age glaciers shaped the valleys and lakes.
Beatrix Potter and William Wordsworth lived here.

abschnitte.text: The Lake District lies in the **north-west of England** in the county of **Cumbria**. Since **1951** it has been a **national park**. In **2017** it was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List as a **cultural landscape**. This protects nature and traditional sheep farming together.

In the **ice age** **glaciers** covered the area. They scoured out deep valleys. When the ice melted, the valleys filled with water to form long, narrow **lakes**. Many lakes in Switzerland formed in a similar way. That is why the Lake District, with its mountains and lakes, sometimes feels familiar to Swiss visitors.

The highest mountain in England is **Scafell Pike** at **978 metres**. It lies in the middle of the Lake District. By Swiss standards that is not very high, but the landscape is rugged and often misty. The largest natural lake in England is **Windermere**. It is over 15 kilometres long, but only about 1.5 kilometres wide.

The children's author **Beatrix Potter** lived at **Hill Top** farm in the Lake District. She invented **Peter Rabbit**. She bought a lot of land and later gave it to **nature conservation**. The poet **William Wordsworth** was born in the Lake District and wrote many nature poems there. His poem about the **daffodils** is especially well known.

gewusst: Thanks to Beatrix Potter, large parts of the Lake District are now protected for conservation.
In his poem Wordsworth described a whole field of dancing daffodils by the lakeside.

teile.einleitung: Ivo Andrić was a writer from Bosnia. In 1961 he received the Nobel Prize in Literature. In his novels he tells of the history of Bosnia and of how different peoples and religions lived together.
wichtigste: Ivo Andrić was born in 1892 in Dolac near Travnik in Bosnia.
In 1961 he received the Nobel Prize in Literature.
His best-known book is “The Bridge on the Drina”.
He also worked as a diplomat.
He died in 1975 in Belgrade.

abschnitte.text: Ivo Andrić was born in **1892** in Dolac near **Travnik** in Bosnia. Bosnia then belonged to Austria-Hungary. He grew up in Višegrad on the Drina and later studied at several universities. For a long time he worked as a **diplomat** for the Kingdom of Yugoslavia, in Berlin among other places. After the Second World War he lived in **Belgrade**, where he died in **1975**.

His best-known novel is “**The Bridge on the Drina**”. It tells the story of the old stone bridge in **Višegrad** over several centuries. The bridge stands for the link between people and cultures. Many generations come and go, but the bridge remains. The real bridge was built in the 16th century and is now a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

In **1961** Ivo Andrić received the **Nobel Prize in Literature**. This is one of the most important awards for writers. He was praised for how vividly he described the history and people of his homeland. Another well-known novel by him is called “Bosnian Chronicle” and is set in Travnik. His books have been translated into many languages, including German.

gewusst: To this day Ivo Andrić is the only winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature from the former Yugoslavia.
His birthplace house in Travnik is now a museum.

teile.einleitung: A continental climate prevails in the interior of large landmasses, far from the sea. Typical features are warm summers and very cold winters. In Europe it is found mainly in the east, for example in Russia and Ukraine.
wichtigste: According to Köppen, Moscow has the climate Dfb: cold temperate, damp all year round, with warm summers.
In Moscow there are about 25 degrees between the coldest and the warmest month.
The Siberian High brings icy cold air from the east in winter.
Most precipitation falls in summer.
In spring and autumn, tracks sink into mud in the rasputitsa.
From north to south come taiga, mixed forest, forest steppe and grass steppe.

abschnitte.text: Land heats up quickly in summer and cools down strongly in winter. The sea, on the other hand, evens things out. That is why the differences between summer and winter are especially large far from the sea. In **Moscow** January is on average about minus 6 degrees cold, and July about 19 degrees warm. This **annual range** of about 25 degrees is typically continental. According to Köppen, Moscow has the climate **Dfb**.

In winter the air over the huge Asian mainland cools down strongly. A high-pressure area forms, the **Siberian High**. On its western edge, icy **east winds** blow towards eastern Europe. Without the moderating influence of the Atlantic, the frosty periods last a long time. That is why the **growing season** is shorter than in western Europe at the same latitude.

In the continental climate of eastern Europe, most precipitation falls in **summer**. Then the land heats up strongly, warm air rises, and **showers and thunderstorms** form. The cold winter air, on the other hand, is rather dry. When the snow melts and in the rainy autumn, unpaved tracks turn soft. This muddy season is called **rasputitsa** in Russia and often made travel and military campaigns almost impossible.

North of the **mixed forest**, the **taiga** begins in Russia, a huge coniferous forest with short summers and long winters. Further south, in Ukraine and southern Russia, comes the **forest steppe**, where islands of forest and areas of grass alternate. Even further south the rain is no longer enough for closed forests. There **grass steppe** originally grew, which is now mostly farmland.

Switzerland lies in the transition between maritime and continental climate. The winters here are mostly milder than in Moscow, because air often flows in from the **Atlantic**. In a **bise**, a cold north-east wind, however, you sometimes feel cold air from the east. Then it can get very cold in the Swiss Plateau too.

gewusst: The fertile black earth of the steppe is among the best farmland in the world.
In Yakutsk in Siberia there are almost 60 degrees between the average of the coldest and the warmest month.

teile.einleitung: Milan, in Italian Milano, is a large city in the north of Italy and the capital of Lombardy. It is world famous for fashion, its huge cathedral and the La Scala opera house.
wichtigste: Milan is called Milano in Italian.
The city is the capital of Lombardy, the most populous region in Italy.
Milan Cathedral is among the largest churches in the world.
The opera house Teatro alla Scala is world famous.
In Milan you can see Leonardo da Vinci's mural “The Last Supper”.
From Zurich you travel through the Gotthard Base Tunnel to Milan.

abschnitte.text: In the middle of the city stands **Milan Cathedral**. It is among the largest churches in the world. Building began in the 14th century and lasted several hundred years. The cathedral has very many pointed spires and countless marble figures. On the highest tower stands a golden figure of Mary. You can climb onto the roof and walk around between the spires.

The **Teatro alla Scala** is one of the most famous opera houses in the world. Great singers perform there. In a monastery next to the church of Santa Maria delle Grazie, **Leonardo da Vinci** painted the mural **“The Last Supper”** at the end of the 15th century. It shows Jesus eating with his disciples. Because it is delicate, only a few visitors may go in at a time.

Milan is regarded as a **capital of fashion**. Many well-known fashion houses have their headquarters here, and every year great fashion shows take place. Furniture and design from Milan are also world famous. A magnificent shopping arcade with a glass roof is the **Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II**, right next to the cathedral.

In the **San Siro** stadium **two** big football clubs play: **AC Milan** and **Inter Milan**. When they play against each other, it is called the derby. Then the whole city is in a flutter. In 2026 Milan, together with Cortina d'Ampezzo, hosted the Winter Olympics.

Milan lies not far from the Swiss border. From Zurich the train runs through the **Gotthard Base Tunnel**, which at 57 kilometres is the longest railway tunnel in the world. The **panettone** also comes from Milan, a tall, airy cake with raisins. In Italy and in Ticino it is eaten mainly at Christmas.

gewusst: Milan Cathedral has more statues than almost any other building in the world, several thousand of them.
Thanks to the Gotthard Base Tunnel, the train journey from Zurich to Milan now takes only a little over three hours.

teile.einleitung: Ireland is an island in the Atlantic, west of Great Britain. The largest part is taken up by the Republic of Ireland, while the north-east belongs to the United Kingdom as Northern Ireland. Because of its many green meadows, Ireland is also called “the Emerald Isle”.
wichtigste: Ireland is called “the Emerald Isle”.
It is so green because it rains often and the winters are mild.
The clover leaf, the shamrock, is a symbol of Ireland.
On 17 March people celebrate St Patrick's Day.
The flag of the Republic of Ireland is green, white and orange.
In the Republic of Ireland people pay with euros.
The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland and in the British Isles.

abschnitte.text: It rains often in Ireland, and the winters are mild. This is because of the **Gulf Stream**, a warm ocean current in the Atlantic. As a result grass grows almost all year round, and you see lush **green meadows** everywhere. That is why Ireland is called “the Emerald Isle”. The best-known symbol of the country is the three-leaved **clover**, called the **shamrock** in English. Another emblem is the **harp**, which can be seen on all Irish euro coins.

On **17 March** people celebrate **St Patrick's Day**. On this day they honour Saint **Patrick**, the patron saint of Ireland. He is said to have brought Christianity to Ireland in the 5th century. According to a legend, he used the clover leaf to explain the Christian faith. Today there are big parades on this day, and many people wear green, not only in Ireland but all over the world.

For a long time Ireland belonged to the United Kingdom. In **1922** most of the island became independent as the **Irish Free State**. The north-east stayed with the United Kingdom as **Northern Ireland**. In 1949 the state became the **Republic of Ireland**. Its capital is **Dublin**. The flag has three vertical stripes in green, white and orange. The Republic belongs to the European Union and pays with the **euro**, while in Northern Ireland people pay with pounds.

Ireland has two official languages: **Irish** and English. Irish is an old Celtic language, but in everyday life most people speak English. From Irish legends comes the **leprechaun**, a little goblin and shoemaker. He is said to hide a **pot of gold** at the end of the rainbow. Ireland is also known for its music with fiddle, flute and harp.

The longest river in Ireland and in the whole of the British Isles is the **Shannon**. It is about 360 kilometres long and so a little longer than the Thames in England. On the west coast the **Cliffs of Moher** plunge steeply into the sea, and they are over 200 metres high. Inland there are many lakes and **bogs**. In the past the peat from the bogs was dried and burned for heating.

gewusst: There are naturally no snakes in Ireland. A legend says Saint Patrick drove them out, but in truth they never reached the island after the Ice Age.
Halloween has its roots in an old Celtic festival in Ireland.

teile.einleitung: Liechtenstein is a small principality between Switzerland and Austria. It is closely tied to Switzerland and even uses the Swiss franc. The country has no army of its own.
wichtigste: Liechtenstein borders only Switzerland and Austria.
It is a doubly landlocked country, as otherwise only Uzbekistan is.
The country has 11 municipalities and about 40,000 inhabitants (as of 2024).
Liechtenstein is a principality with a constitution.
The customs treaty of 1923 links it closely with Switzerland.
Since 1868 Liechtenstein has had no army.

abschnitte.titel: Small and in the middle of the Alps
abschnitte.text: Liechtenstein lies between **Switzerland** and **Austria** and has only these two neighbouring countries. The border with Switzerland is formed mostly by the **Rhine**. The main town is **Vaduz**. The country consists of only **11 municipalities**. In 2024 about **40,000 people** lived there, roughly as many as in the town of Thun.

A **landlocked country** is a country with no access to the sea. Liechtenstein is even **doubly landlocked**: its neighbours, Switzerland and Austria, have no sea either. Anyone who wants to get from Liechtenstein to the sea must therefore cross at least two borders. Besides Liechtenstein there is only one other country in the world in this position: **Uzbekistan** in Central Asia.

Liechtenstein is a **principality** with a **constitution**. The head of state is the **prince**, at present Prince **Hans-Adam II**. Since **2004** his son, **Hereditary Prince Alois**, has run the business of government for him. There is also a parliament elected by the people, the **Landtag**. As in Switzerland, the people can also vote on issues.

With the **customs treaty** of **1923**, Switzerland and Liechtenstein form a shared **customs area**. That is why there are no customs checks between the two countries. Liechtenstein uses the **Swiss franc** as its currency. Many people from Austria and Switzerland travel to work in Liechtenstein every day.
Liechtenstein used to have a small **army**. In **1868** it was disbanded. Since then the country has been **without a military**. Security inside the country is provided by the national police.

gewusst: Liechtenstein and Uzbekistan are the only doubly landlocked countries in the world.
Liechtenstein has had no army for over 150 years.

teile.einleitung: Yugoslavia was a state in the Balkans in the south-east of Europe. It existed from 1918 until the 1990s and united several South Slavic peoples. From 1991 it broke up into several independent countries.
wichtigste: The name Yugoslavia means “land of the South Slavs”.
The state came into being in 1918 after the First World War, at first as a kingdom.
After the Second World War it became the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.
For a long time Josip Broz Tito ruled the country.
Yugoslavia consisted of six constituent republics.
From 1991 the state broke up, accompanied by wars.
Among the results were Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and North Macedonia.

abschnitte.text: After the First World War, in 1918, Serbs, Croats and Slovenes joined together in a common **kingdom**. From 1929 it was officially called the Kingdom of Yugoslavia. In the Second World War the country was occupied by Germany and its allies. Resistance fighters, the **Partisans**, fought against the occupiers.

After the war the Partisan leader **Josip Broz Tito** took power. Yugoslavia became a socialist state with a single party. Unlike many countries in eastern Europe, however, it did not follow the Soviet Union. It was one of the founders of the **Non-Aligned Movement**, whose members did not want to join either of the great power blocs.

The federal state consisted of six **constituent republics**: Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Montenegro and Macedonia. Serbia also included the provinces of Vojvodina and Kosovo. Many peoples with different languages and religions lived in Yugoslavia. People wrote with both Latin and Cyrillic letters.

After Tito's death in 1980, tensions between the republics grew, and the economy fell into crisis. In 1991 **Slovenia** and **Croatia** declared their independence, and other republics soon followed. The **Yugoslav Wars** broke out, in which many people died or had to flee. Serbia and Montenegro stayed together for a while longer and separated in 2006.

From the 1960s onwards, many people from Yugoslavia came to Switzerland as **workers**. During the wars of the 1990s many refugees also found protection here. Today many families with roots in the successor states of Yugoslavia live in Switzerland. They also help to shape Switzerland in sport, culture and everyday life.

gewusst: The languages Serbian, Croatian, Bosnian and Montenegrin are so similar that people understand each other well.
Sarajevo, the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina, hosted the Winter Olympics in 1984.

teile.einleitung: The Louvre in Paris is one of the largest art museums in the world. It used to be a royal palace, and today the famous Mona Lisa hangs there, among other works.
wichtigste: The Louvre is a huge art museum in Paris.
It is the most visited museum in the world, with about 9 million visitors in 2024.
It used to be a fortress and later a palace of the French kings.
Since 1793 it has been a museum for everyone.
In front of the entrance stands a large glass pyramid.
Among the best-known works are the Mona Lisa and the Venus de Milo.

abschnitte.text: The Louvre began around the year 1200 as a **fortress** to protect Paris. Later the kings rebuilt it into a magnificent **palace** and lived there. When the kings moved to Versailles, many works of art stayed behind in the Louvre. In **1793**, during the French Revolution, it was opened as a museum for everyone.

In front of the Louvre stands a large **pyramid of glass** and metal. It was finished in 1989 and comes from the architect Ieoh Ming Pei. At first some people found it too modern for the old palace. Today it is a landmark of Paris itself. Under the pyramid lies the main entrance, from which you reach the various wings of the museum.

The most famous painting in the Louvre is the **Mona Lisa** by Leonardo da Vinci. It shows a woman with a mysterious smile. The painting is smaller than many expect, and very valuable. That is why it hangs behind thick **bulletproof glass** that can even withstand blows. Every day many people stand in front of it to see it.

The Louvre shows not only paintings, but also statues and treasures from ancient cultures, for example from Egypt, Greece and the Orient. The **Venus de Milo** is a marble statue from ancient Greece. Its arms were already missing when it was found. Also famous is the **Winged Victory of Samothrace**, a winged goddess of victory who stands at the top of a large staircase.

The Louvre is the **most visited museum in the world**. In 2024 about 9 million people came. The building is so large that it is impossible to see everything in a single day. Many visitors therefore choose beforehand which works interest them most.

gewusst: Anyone who wanted to look at each work of art in the Louvre only briefly would be busy for many weeks.
The Mona Lisa is only about 77 centimetres high and 53 centimetres wide.

teile.einleitung: The North Atlantic is the northern part of the Atlantic Ocean between Europe and North America. It strongly shapes the weather and climate in Europe, including in Switzerland.
wichtigste: After the Pacific, the Atlantic is the second largest ocean on Earth.
The warm North Atlantic Current keeps many ports in Norway ice-free in winter.
Because of the sea, western Europe has a balanced maritime climate.
The Azores High and the Icelandic Low strongly determine the weather in Europe.
Iceland lies on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
In 1912 the Titanic sank in the North Atlantic after a collision with an iceberg.

abschnitte.text: After the Pacific, the **Atlantic Ocean** is the **second largest ocean** on Earth. It covers about a fifth of the Earth's surface. It separates **Europe and Africa** from the **Americas**. The northern part is called the **North Atlantic**. There lie islands such as Iceland, Ireland and Great Britain.

Through the North Atlantic flows the warm **North Atlantic Current**. It brings warmth from the south far to the north. That is why many ports on the coast of **Norway** stay **ice-free** in winter despite their northern position. Water stores heat well and releases it slowly to the air. Westerly winds bring this evening-out sea air onto the land. This is called a **maritime climate**: milder winters and cooler summers.

Over the North Atlantic there are two important areas of air pressure. In the south lies the **Azores High**, an area of high air pressure. In the north lies the **Icelandic Low** with low air pressure. Between them blow **westerly winds**, which bring the weather from the Atlantic to Europe. Many rain fronts that move into **Switzerland** also come from there.

On the floor of the Atlantic runs a long mountain range, the **Mid-Atlantic Ridge**. There two **tectonic plates** are drifting apart, the North American and the Eurasian plate. **Iceland** lies right on this ridge. There the plates move away from each other by about **2 centimetres** every year. That is why Iceland has many volcanoes and hot springs.

In **1912** the **Titanic** sank on her first voyage from England to New York. She had collided with an **iceberg** south-east of **Newfoundland**. The Atlantic shows quite a different face in **Ireland**: damp air brings a lot of rain, and the mild winters let the grass grow almost all year. That is why Ireland is called the **Emerald Isle**.

gewusst: The Atlantic grows a little wider every year, at about the speed at which fingernails grow.
Icebergs in the North Atlantic come mainly from the glaciers of Greenland.

teile.einleitung: Luxembourg is a small country between Belgium, France and Germany. It is the only grand duchy in the world, and its capital is also called Luxembourg.
wichtigste: Luxembourg is the only grand duchy in the world.
The capital has the same name as the country: Luxembourg.
The official languages are Luxembourgish, French and German.
The country borders Belgium, France and Germany.
It is about 16 times smaller than Switzerland.
Since 2020 buses, trams and trains have been free across the whole country.

abschnitte.text: Luxembourg is the **only grand duchy** in the world. At its head stands a **grand duke**, but the government and parliament make the policy, much as with a king in other countries. Luxembourg borders **Belgium**, **France** and **Germany**. It is about 16 times smaller than Switzerland and roughly as large as the canton of Ticino.

Among themselves people speak **Luxembourgish**, a language related to German. **French** and **German** are also official languages. Children learn all three at school. Many Luxembourgers switch effortlessly between languages in everyday life, much as some people do in the bilingual town of Biel.

The capital, **Luxembourg**, lies on rocks above deep valleys. In the past it was a mighty **fortress**. Deep in the rock soldiers dug long tunnels, the **casemates**, in which they could shelter. Today you can visit part of them. The old town and the remains of the fortress are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Important institutions of the European Union are also based in the city.

In the south of Luxembourg, **iron ore** was mined in the 19th and 20th centuries and made into **steel**. The company **Arbed** was one of the largest steel producers in the world. This made the country wealthy. Later banks and other services became more important. Every day many people from the neighbouring countries come to work in Luxembourg.

Since 2020 you can travel across the whole of Luxembourg by bus, tram and train **without a ticket**. Luxembourg was the first country in the world to make public transport free across the whole country. The **flag** has three horizontal stripes of red, white and light blue. It looks similar to the flag of the Netherlands, only the blue is lighter.

gewusst: Luxembourg is one of the six countries that founded the forerunners of today's EU in the 1950s.
In Luxembourg you do not have to buy a ticket on buses and trains, except in first class.

teile.einleitung: The joik is the traditional singing of the Sami. The Sami are a people in the far north of Europe, in Norway, Sweden, Finland and Russia. A joik is used to sing about a person, an animal or a landscape.
wichtigste: The joik is the traditional singing of the Sami.
The Sami live in the north of Norway, Sweden, Finland and Russia.
A joik describes a person, an animal or a landscape.
It is one of the oldest music traditions in Europe.
For a long time the joik was forbidden or frowned upon.

abschnitte.text: A **joik** is a song that you use to sing about someone or something: a person, an animal such as the reindeer, or a landscape. People say you do not sing about a person, but you “joik” them. The joik is meant to capture the nature of that person or place, almost like a picture made of sounds. Often it has only a few words or none at all. Traditionally it is sung without instruments.

The **Sami** live in the north of Scandinavia and on the Russian Kola Peninsula. They call their region **Sápmi**. In the past many of them lived from **reindeer herding**, fishing and hunting. They have their own languages and their own culture. The joik is one of the oldest **music traditions** in Europe.

For a long time the joik was rejected by churchmen, because they thought it was pagan. In some places it was even forbidden, and joiking was not allowed in schools either. As a result a lot of knowledge was lost. Since the 20th century the joik has been proudly kept alive again. Today musicians also combine it with pop, rock and other modern music.

gewusst: A joik often belongs entirely to one person, and sometimes you are given it as a gift while still a child.

teile.einleitung: Lisbon is the capital of Portugal and lies where the Tagus flows into the Atlantic. The city is known for its steep lanes, yellow trams and colourful tiles. In 1755 a severe earthquake destroyed large parts of the city.
wichtigste: Lisbon is the capital of Portugal and lies on the Tagus.
It is called the city of seven hills.
On 1 November 1755 an earthquake, a tsunami and fires destroyed large parts of the city.
The yellow tram line 28 is world famous.
Fado is an emotional style of singing and a UNESCO cultural heritage.
Many houses are decorated with painted tiles, the azulejos.

abschnitte.text: **Lisbon** is the capital of **Portugal**. It lies where the **Tagus** flows into the **Atlantic**, and the river is very wide here. Lisbon is often called the **city of seven hills**. That is why there are many steep lanes and stairs. Small **yellow trams** run through the narrow lanes, and **line 28** is especially well known.

On **1 November 1755** the ground shook very strongly in Lisbon. Afterwards came a **tsunami**, a huge wave, and great **fires**. Large parts of the city were destroyed, and many people lost their lives. Afterwards the lower town, the **Baixa**, was rebuilt with straight streets. The earthquake moved people all over Europe at the time.

The **Belém Tower** was built about 500 years ago right on the bank of the Tagus. It was meant to protect the entrance to the **harbour**. Over the river runs the red suspension bridge, the **25 de Abril Bridge**. It looks similar to the **Golden Gate Bridge** in San Francisco.

**Fado** is an emotional, often sad style of singing from Lisbon. It is mostly accompanied by **guitars** and is part of the **UNESCO cultural heritage**. Many house walls are decorated with colourful, often blue and white tiles. These tiles are called **azulejos** and at the same time protect the walls from the weather.

Especially popular are the **pastéis de nata**. These are small tarts of **puff pastry**, filled with a cream similar to custard. They are often eaten warm and sprinkled with **cinnamon**. You can also buy them in some bakeries in Switzerland.

gewusst: The 25 de Abril Bridge in Lisbon looks almost like the Golden Gate Bridge.
After the earthquake of 1755 a whole district was newly planned with perfectly straight streets.

teile.einleitung: Musala is the highest mountain in Bulgaria and on the whole Balkan Peninsula. It lies in the Rila Mountains in the south-west of Bulgaria.
wichtigste: Musala is 2925 metres high.
It is the highest mountain on the Balkan Peninsula.
It lies in the Bulgarian Rila Mountains.
It is slightly higher than Mount Olympus in Greece.
On the summit stands a weather station.

abschnitte.text: **Musala** is **2925 metres** high. That makes it the highest mountain in **Bulgaria** and on the whole **Balkan Peninsula**. The famous **Mount Olympus** in Greece is only a few metres lower. Musala lies in the **Rila Mountains** south of the capital, Sofia.

The **Rila Mountains** are the highest range in Bulgaria. They have many clear **glacial lakes**, for example the well-known Seven Rila Lakes. Important rivers rise in the mountains. Also well known is the **Rila Monastery**, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Musala is popular with **hikers**. A common starting point is the winter sports resort of **Borovets**. From there a cable car goes part of the way up, and then you continue on foot. On the summit stands a **weather station**, and in clear weather the view reaches far over the mountains.

gewusst: From 1949 to 1962 Musala for a time bore a different name, after which it got its old name back.

teile.einleitung: Kronborg is a famous castle in Denmark, north of Copenhagen. It stands in the town of Helsingør and is the setting of Shakespeare's play “Hamlet”.
wichtigste: Kronborg Castle stands in Helsingør in Denmark.
It lies at the narrowest point of the Øresund.
In Shakespeare's “Hamlet” the action takes place in this castle.
Kronborg is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The castle was extended in the Renaissance style in the 16th century.

abschnitte.text: Kronborg stands in **Helsingør**, at the narrowest point of the **Øresund**. The Øresund is the strait between Denmark and Sweden. On the other side you can see the Swedish town of Helsingborg. In the 16th century the castle was magnificently extended in the **Renaissance** style. It is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

Anyone who wanted to sail from the North Sea into the Baltic had to pass through the Øresund. That is why the Danish king demanded a **toll** here for a long time, the **Sound Dues**. Ships had to stop in front of Kronborg and pay. The castle's cannons made sure that nobody simply sailed past. The Sound Dues were abolished in the 19th century.

The English poet **William Shakespeare** set his play **“Hamlet”** in Helsingør. It is about a Danish prince. That is why Kronborg is known all over the world as **Hamlet's castle**. The play is performed again and again in the castle courtyard, often by theatre groups from many countries.

gewusst: In the cellar vaults of Kronborg sits a statue of Holger Danske, a hero from a Danish legend, who according to the story will awaken when Denmark is in danger.

teile.einleitung: The Lovćen is a mountain range in Montenegro above the old capital Cetinje. On one of its peaks stands the tomb of Petar II Petrović-Njegoš, a ruler and poet.
wichtigste: The Lovćen lies in Montenegro, above the town of Cetinje.
The range is a national park and a symbol of the country.
On one peak stands the mausoleum of Petar II Petrović-Njegoš.
In the 19th century Njegoš was a ruler, a bishop and a poet.
From the summit you can see as far as the Adriatic in clear weather.

abschnitte.text: The Lovćen rises not far from the Adriatic coast, above the Bay of **Kotor**. On the other side lies **Cetinje**, the old capital of Montenegro. The range is a **national park** with forests, karst rocks and hiking trails. From the top, in clear weather, the view reaches over mountains and as far as the sea.

**Petar II Petrović-Njegoš** lived from 1813 to 1851. He was a prince-bishop, that is, a secular ruler and head of the Church at the same time. To this day he is known above all as a **poet**. His work “The Mountain Wreath” is regarded as one of the most important books in the literature of Montenegro and Serbia. He wished to be buried on the Lovćen.

Today a large **mausoleum**, a magnificent tomb, stands on a peak of the Lovćen. It was designed by the sculptor **Ivan Meštrović** and finished in the 1970s. Visitors climb first through a tunnel and then up many steps. For many people in Montenegro the place is an important **symbol** of their country.

gewusst: It is thought that the dark, forested Lovćen helped to give Montenegro its name, which means “Black Mountain”.

teile.einleitung: The Cyrillic alphabet is a script used to write many languages in eastern Europe and Asia, for example Russian. It is named after the missionary Cyril. Many of its letters come from the Greek alphabet.
wichtigste: The script is named after Cyril, the 9th-century “Apostle to the Slavs”.
Russian is written in Cyrillic and has 33 letters.
Many Cyrillic letters come from the Greek alphabet.
Bulgaria is the EU country with an official Cyrillic script.
Serbian can be written in Cyrillic and in Latin letters.
Polish is a Slavic language but is written in Latin letters.

abschnitte.text: In the **9th century** the brothers **Cyril** and **Methodius** went to the Slavs as missionaries. They wanted to translate the Bible into the Slavic language. For that a script of its own was needed. Soon afterwards the **Cyrillic alphabet** developed from this work, named after Cyril. That is why Cyril is also called the **Apostle to the Slavs**.

Many Cyrillic letters were taken over from the **Greek alphabet**, for example **Г** for G or **П** for P. For sounds that did not exist in Greek, new signs were added. Some letters look like Latin ones but sound different. The **“Р”** looks like a P but is pronounced like **R**. **Ш** sounds like “sh”, and **Ж** like the s in “measure”.

**Russian** is written in the Cyrillic alphabet, which has **33 letters** there. Ukrainian, Belarusian, **Bulgarian**, Macedonian and Serbian also use this script, as do languages in Asia such as Mongolian. **Serbian** can be written in both Cyrillic and Latin letters. **Polish**, Czech, Slovenian and Croatian are also Slavic languages, but are written only in Latin letters.

When **Bulgaria** joined the EU in **2007**, Cyrillic became the **third script** of the EU, alongside Latin and Greek. That is why the word euro also appears in Cyrillic letters on the newer **euro banknotes**: **ЕВРО**. This has been the case since the second series of banknotes.

gewusst: On euro notes the word euro appears in three scripts: Latin, Greek and Cyrillic.
The letter Щ is pronounced “shch”, a single sign for several English letters.

teile.einleitung: The Cyclades are a group of islands in the Aegean Sea that belong to Greece. Their name comes from the Greek word for circle. Thousands of years ago people lived here who made famous marble figures.
wichtigste: “Kyklos” means circle: the islands lie roughly in a circle around the holy island of Delos.
Naxos is the largest and highest island of the Cyclades.
On Milos the statue “Venus de Milo” was found in 1820.
The administrative capital Ermoupoli lies on the island of Syros.
Paros was famous in antiquity for its fine white marble.
The Cycladic idols are about 4500 years old.

abschnitte.text: The Cyclades lie in the **Aegean Sea**, the sea between Greece and Turkey. The name comes from the Greek word **“Kyklos”**, which means **circle**. The islands lie roughly in a circle around the small island of **Delos**. The group includes dozens of islands, many of them uninhabited. Well known are, for example, **Naxos**, **Paros**, **Mykonos** and **Santorini**.

In antiquity Delos was a **holy island**. According to Greek legend, the goddess **Leto** gave birth here to the twins **Apollo** and **Artemis**. That is why the Greeks built many temples on Delos. Today the island is almost uninhabited, but full of excavations, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

In the **Bronze Age** the **Cycladic culture** flourished on the islands. Its people made flat, strongly simplified figures of **marble**, the **Cycladic idols**. They are about **4500 years** old and recall modern art. The island of **Paros** was famous for its especially fine, slightly translucent **marble**. It was partly quarried in underground tunnels and used for many statues.

In **1820** a farmer on the island of **Milos** found a marble statue of a goddess. It became world famous as the **“Venus de Milo”**, although both its arms are missing. Today it stands in the **Louvre** in Paris. It is one of the best-known works of art from antiquity.

**Naxos**, with about 430 square kilometres, is the largest Cycladic island and also the highest. On **Syros** lies **Ermoupoli**, the administrative capital of the region. In the 19th century Ermoupoli was the most important port city in Greece. **Santorini** is the remains of a volcano that erupted enormously in the Bronze Age.

gewusst: The Cycladic idols are so plain that they inspired artists of the 20th century.
The island of Santorini has the shape of a ring because it is the rim of a collapsed volcano.

teile.einleitung: Austria is a country in central Europe and a neighbour of Switzerland. A large part of the country lies in the Alps. The capital is Vienna on the Danube.
wichtigste: Austria borders eight countries, including Switzerland and Liechtenstein.
It is about twice as large as Switzerland.
The capital is Vienna, and the country has nine federal states.
With the State Treaty of 15 May 1955 Austria became fully independent again.
The national holiday is on 26 October.
Since 1995 Austria has belonged to the European Union.

abschnitte.text: Austria borders **eight countries**: Germany, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Italy, Switzerland and Liechtenstein. At about 83,900 square kilometres it is about **twice as large** as Switzerland. The country is a **federal state** with nine federal states, much as Switzerland has cantons.

About two thirds of the country lie in the **Alps**. The highest mountain is the **Grossglockner** at 3798 metres. Through the north flows the **Danube**. The **Inn** comes from the Engadine in Switzerland and flows through Tyrol. Between Braunau and Passau it forms the border with Bavaria, and at Passau it flows into the Danube.

After the Second World War Austria was occupied for ten years by four **victorious powers**. With the **Austrian State Treaty** of 15 May 1955 it regained its full independence, and the troops left. On 26 October 1955 parliament decided on **permanent neutrality**. Since 1965 this day has been the national holiday.
