At Lichterfeld stands the overburden conveyor bridge **F60**, more than 500 metres long, the **“lying Eiffel Tower”**, today a visitor mine.

gewusst: The conveyor bridge F60 is among the largest movable machines in the world.
Where coal used to be mined, you can now swim and sail.

teile.einleitung: Majorca is the largest island of the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean and belongs to Spain. The island is one of the most popular holiday destinations in Europe, with beaches, mountains and the capital Palma.
wichtigste: Majorca belongs to the Balearic Islands and so to Spain.
Minorca and Ibiza also belong to the Balearic Islands.
The highest mountain is Puig Major at about 1445 metres.
The Serra de Tramuntana in the north-west is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
In Palma the cathedral La Seu stands right on the sea.
An old train, the “Red Lightning”, has run to Sóller since 1912.

abschnitte.titel: The largest of the Balearic Islands
abschnitte.text: Majorca is the largest island of the **Balearic Islands**, a group of islands in the western Mediterranean. They also include **Minorca**, the smaller neighbouring island to the east, and **Ibiza**. The Balearic Islands belong to **Spain**. As well as Spanish, people on Majorca also speak **Catalan**, which is called Majorcan here.

Along the north-west coast runs the mountain range **Serra de Tramuntana**. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. There too lies the highest mountain on the island, **Puig Major**, at about 1445 metres. Right in the north a long, rocky peninsula ends at **Cap de Formentor** with a lighthouse. This is the northernmost point of Majorca.

The capital, **Palma**, lies on a large bay in the south. On a rise by the harbour stands the Gothic **cathedral La Seu**, which can be seen from far away. From Palma an old train with wood-panelled carriages has run through the mountains to **Sóller** since 1912. German-speaking holidaymakers call it the **“Red Lightning”**.

Every year millions of visitors come to Majorca, especially in summer. Most land at **Son Sant Joan** airport near Palma, one of the busiest airports in Spain. A stretch of beach at the Playa de Palma is known as **Ballermann**. The name goes back to a beach kiosk. Because there is a lot of partying and drinking there, the city of Palma has introduced stricter rules.

A well-known pastry of the island is the **ensaïmada**, a soft yeast pastry twisted into a spiral. Its name comes from “saïm”, the pork lard in the dough. On the island grow many almond, olive and orange trees. In spring blossoming almond trees turn whole valleys into a sea of white and pink flowers.

gewusst: The cathedral La Seu has one of the largest round church windows in the world.
The “Red Lightning” runs through several tunnels to get over the mountains of the Tramuntana.

teile.einleitung: The Isle of Wight is the largest island of England. It lies in the English Channel off the south coast, opposite Southampton and Portsmouth. It is known for its chalk cliffs, sailing regattas and finds of dinosaurs.
wichtigste: The Isle of Wight is the largest island of England.
It lies in the English Channel off Southampton.
Ferries link it with the mainland.
The white chalk cliffs “The Needles” are its landmark.
Queen Victoria had her summer residence Osborne House here.

abschnitte.text: The Isle of Wight lies in the **English Channel** off the south coast of England. Between the island and the mainland lies a strait, the **Solent**. There is no bridge, so people cross by **ferry** from Southampton, Portsmouth or Lymington. Between Portsmouth and the island there is even a **hovercraft**. The island is very popular with holidaymakers and sailors.

Right in the west, the **Needles** stick out of the sea, three pointed rocks of white **chalk**. A lighthouse stands next to them. On the island's coasts the rock keeps crumbling away. As it does so, many **fossils** come to light, including bones and footprints of **dinosaurs**. That is why the Isle of Wight is regarded as one of the best places in Europe to find dinosaur remains.

The British **Queen Victoria** had **Osborne House** built on the island as a summer residence. She spent a lot of time there with her family and died in this house in 1901. Today you can visit it. The town of **Cowes** is world famous for sailing. Every summer one of the largest sailing regattas in the world, **Cowes Week**, takes place there.

gewusst: On the Isle of Wight, old carriages that were once used on the London Underground run as suburban trains.
